normalization.note: Neither tokenizer has a normalizer (tokenizer.json 'normalizer' is null; tiktoken applies none), so the two Unicode forms of the same visible word give different IDs.

k3.rule: encoding_k3.py encodes user and tool text with disallowed_special=(), so spelled control tokens stay plain text; only the renderer's own markers become control tokens.

mistral.rule: tokenizers parses added special tokens inside any string by default; setting encode_special_tokens=True encodes them as ordinary text.

merge_trace.rule: start from single bytes; repeatedly merge the adjacent pair whose concatenation has the lowest rank in tiktoken.model; stop when no adjacent pair is in the vocabulary
